items.informal_name: Degree Bound for Multivariate Polynomials in Chevalley's Theorem
items.type: ℕ → (ℕ → ℕ) → ℕ → ℕ
items.informal_description: A function that computes a degree bound for multivariate polynomials, taking a natural number $n$, a function $f : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$, and an element of the sum type $\mathbb{N} \oplus \mathbb{N}$. For left components, it applies $f$ to $n$, and for right components, it returns $n$ directly. This is used in the proof of Chevalley's theorem to establish well-founded recursion for multivariate polynomial constructions.

items.informal_name: Degree Bound for Chevalley's Theorem Using Multiset of Finite Elements
items.type: ℕ → (m : ℕ) → ℕ → Multiset (Fin m) → ℕ
items.informal_description: The function computes a degree bound for Chevalley's theorem by taking $k + n$ and a function that adds 1 to the count of each natural number obtained from mapping $\text{Fin.val}$ over the multiset $d$ of type $\text{Fin} \, m$. This constructs a degree bound used in the proof of Chevalley's theorem for multivariate polynomial recursions.

items.informal_name: Numerical Bound for Multivariate Polynomials in Chevalley's Theorem
items.type: ℕ → (ℕ → ℕ) → ℕ → ℕ
items.informal_description: A function that takes a natural number $n$, a function $f : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$, and another natural number $m$, returning a natural number used to establish well-founded recursion in the context of multivariate polynomials and Chevalley's theorem. It computes bounds by recursively applying $f$ to $n$ and decrementing $m$.

items.informal_name: Recursive Successor Formula for Degree Bound in Chevalley's Theorem
items.type:
∀ (k : ℕ) (D : ℕ → ℕ) (n : ℕ),
  ChevalleyThm.MvPolynomialC.degBound k D (n + 1) =
    ChevalleyThm.MvPolynomialC.numBound k D (n + 1) ^ ChevalleyThm.MvPolynomialC.numBound k D (n + 1) *
      ChevalleyThm.MvPolynomialC.degBound k D n
items.informal_description: For natural numbers $k$, $D$, and $n$, the degree bound $\operatorname{degBound}(k, D, n+1)$ satisfies the recursive relation $\operatorname{degBound}(k, D, n+1) = \operatorname{numBound}(k, D, n+1)^{\operatorname{numBound}(k, D, n+1)} \cdot \operatorname{degBound}(k, D, n)$, where $\operatorname{numBound}$ computes numerical bounds for multivariate polynomials in the context of Chevalley's theorem.

items.informal_name: Degree Bound for Hasse Derivative of Polynomials
items.type:
∀ {R : Type u_1} [inst : Semiring R] (p : Polynomial R) (n : ℕ),
  ((Polynomial.hasseDeriv n) p).natDegree ≤ p.natDegree - n
items.informal_description: For any polynomial $ p $ over a semiring $ R $ and any natural number $ n $, the natural degree of the $ n $-th Hasse derivative of $ p $ satisfies $ \deg(D^{(n)}(p)) \leq \deg(p) - n $, where $ D^{(n)} $ denotes the Hasse derivative of order $ n $.

items.informal_name: Natural Degree of Determinant of X•A + B is Bounded by Index Type Cardinality
items.type:
∀ {n : Type u_1} {α : Type u_2} [inst : DecidableEq n] [inst_1 : Fintype n] [inst_2 : CommRing α] (A B : Matrix n n α),
  (Polynomial.X • A.map ⇑Polynomial.C + B.map ⇑Polynomial.C).det.natDegree ≤ Fintype.card n
items.informal_description: For any commutative ring $\alpha$ and finite type $n$, and for any $n \times n$ matrices $A$ and $B$ with entries in $\alpha$, the natural degree of the determinant of the matrix $X \cdot A + B$ (where $X$ is the indeterminate and entries are embedded as constant polynomials) is at most the cardinality of $n$.

items.informal_name: Total Degree of Matrix Row Polynomial is At Most One
items.type:
∀ {m : Type u_1} {n : Type u_2} {R : Type u_4} [inst : Fintype n] [inst_1 : CommSemiring R] (M : Matrix m n R) (i : m),
  (M.toMvPolynomial i).totalDegree ≤ 1
items.informal_description: For any matrix $ M $ with entries in a commutative semiring $ R $ and any row index $ i $, the total degree of the multivariate polynomial constructed from the $ i $-th row of $ M $ is at most 1. This polynomial is defined as the linear combination $ \sum_j M_{i,j} x_j $, where each term corresponds to a column entry multiplied by its respective variable.

items.informal_name: Determinant of a Matrix of Monic Polynomials with Degree Conditions Equals One
items.type:
∀ {R : Type v} [inst : CommRing R] {n : ℕ} (p : Fin n → Polynomial R),
  (∀ (i : Fin n), (p i).natDegree = ↑i) → (∀ (i : Fin n), (p i).Monic) → (Matrix.of fun i j => (p j).coeff ↑i).det = 1
items.informal_description: For a commutative ring $ R $ and natural number $ n $, consider monic polynomials $ p_0, p_1, \ldots, p_{n-1} $ in $ R[X] $ where each $ p_i $ has degree $ i $. Construct an $ n \times n $ matrix $ M $ such that the entry in row $ i $ and column $ j $ is the coefficient of $ X^i $ in $ p_j $. Then the determinant of $ M $ is equal to 1.

items.informal_name: Natural Degree Bound for Characteristic Matrix Entries
items.type:
∀ {R : Type u} [inst : CommRing R] {n : Type v} [inst_1 : DecidableEq n] [inst_2 : Fintype n] {M : Matrix n n R}
  (i j : n), (M.charmatrix i j).natDegree ≤ if i = j then 1 else 0
items.informal_description: For a matrix $ M $ over a commutative ring with finite index type $ n $, the natural degree of the polynomial entry at position $ (i,j) $ in the characteristic matrix $ tI - M $ satisfies: it is at most $ 1 $ if $ i = j $, and at most $ 0 $ otherwise.

items.informal_name: Leading Coefficient of Determinant of $ XA + B $ is Determinant of $ A $
items.type:
∀ {n : Type u_1} {α : Type u_2} [inst : DecidableEq n] [inst_1 : Fintype n] [inst_2 : CommRing α] (A B : Matrix n n α),
  (Polynomial.X • A.map ⇑Polynomial.C + B.map ⇑Polynomial.C).det.coeff (Fintype.card n) = A.det
items.informal_description: For square matrices $ A $ and $ B $ over a commutative ring $ \alpha $, the coefficient of $ X^{\#n} $ in the determinant of the matrix $ X \cdot A + B $ (where entries are lifted to polynomials via constant embedding) is equal to the determinant of $ A $. Here $ \#n $ denotes the cardinality of the finite type $ n $.

items.informal_name: Non-vanishing Determinant of Square Matrix of Variables in Multivariate Polynomial Ring
items.type:
∀ (m : Type u_1) (R : Type u_3) [inst : DecidableEq m] [inst_1 : Fintype m] [inst_2 : CommRing R] [Nontrivial R],
  (Matrix.mvPolynomialX m m R).det ≠ 0
items.informal_description: Given a finite type $ m $ with decidable equality and a non-trivial commutative ring $ R $, the determinant of the $ m \times m $ matrix whose $(i,j)$-entries are distinct indeterminates $ X_{(i,j)} $ in the multivariate polynomial ring $ R[X_{(i,j)}] $ is non-zero. This holds because the determinant evaluates to a monomial that cannot be zero in the polynomial ring over a non-trivial ring.

  (Matrix.mvPolynomialX m m R).det ≠ 0
items.informal_description: Given a finite type $ m $ with decidable equality and a non-trivial commutative ring $ R $, the determinant of the $ m \times m $ matrix whose $(i,j)$-entries are distinct indeterminates $ X_{(i,j)} $ in the multivariate polynomial ring $ R[X_{(i,j)}] $ is non-zero. This holds because the determinant evaluates to a monomial that cannot be zero in the polynomial ring over a non-trivial ring.

items.informal_name: Leading Coefficient of Determinant of $ XA + B $ is Determinant of $ A $
items.type:
∀ {n : Type u_1} {α : Type u_2} [inst : DecidableEq n] [inst_1 : Fintype n] [inst_2 : CommRing α] (A B : Matrix n n α),
  (Polynomial.X • A.map ⇑Polynomial.C + B.map ⇑Polynomial.C).det.coeff (Fintype.card n) = A.det
items.informal_description: For square matrices $ A $ and $ B $ over a commutative ring $ \alpha $, the coefficient of $ X^{\#n} $ in the determinant of the matrix $ X \cdot A + B $ (where entries are lifted to polynomials via constant embedding) is equal to the determinant of $ A $. Here $ \#n $ denotes the cardinality of the finite type $ n $.

items.informal_name: Vandermonde Determinant Equals Monic Polynomial Evaluation Determinant
items.type:
∀ {R : Type u_1} [inst : CommRing R] {n : ℕ} (v : Fin n → R) (p : Fin n → Polynomial R),
  (∀ (i : Fin n), (p i).natDegree = ↑i) →
    (∀ (i : Fin n), (p i).Monic) → (Matrix.vandermonde v).det = (Matrix.of fun i j => Polynomial.eval (v i) (p j)).det
items.informal_description: For a commutative ring $ R $, a vector $ v $ of length $ n $ with entries in $ R $, and a sequence of monic polynomials $ p_0, p_1, \ldots, p_{n-1} $ over $ R $ where each $ p_i $ has degree $ i $, the determinant of the $ n \times n $ Vandermonde matrix formed by $ v $ is equal to the determinant of the matrix whose $ (i,j) $-entry is $ p_j(v_i) $, the evaluation of polynomial $ p_j $ at $ v_i $. This equality holds under the conditions that each polynomial is monic and has natural degree equal to its index.
